jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a newly created executive role at The Open Door Network — and one of the most consequential hires the organization will make. TODN is a Bakersfield\-based nonprofit with over 200 employees supporting victim advocacy, homeless services, trauma\-informed care, medical respite, workforce development, childcare, and clinical services across multiple sites, including a new four\-building shelter campus at 529 Dolores Street.

Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO will own the internal operational leadership of the organization — overseeing programs and grants and data — so the CEO can remain focused on external strategy, board governance, the capital campaign, and community relationships.

This is a hands\-on executive role for a seasoned operator who thrives in complex, mission\-driven environments. The COO will serve as a trusted operational partner to the CEO, building the systems, structures, and accountability culture TODN needs to sustain and accelerate its growth.

**What You’ll Do**

**Operational Leadership**

● Provide day\-to\-day executive oversight of TODN’s program and grants functions

● Partner closely with the CEO to advance organizational priorities, taking ownership of internal operations so the CEO can remain focused on external leadership and mission growth

● Build and maintain a culture of accountability, transparency, and high performance across all departments

● Lead cross\-functional coordination to eliminate silos and ensure alignment across a multi\-site, multi\-program organization

● Represent the CEO internally and with key operational partners as delegated

● Willingness to work evenings and weekends as needed to attend internal and external events, community functions, and organizational activities

**Programs Oversight**

● Supervise the Director of Programs and provide strategic and operational guidance across TODN’s full service continuum: victim advocacy, homeless services, trauma\-informed care, medical respite, workforce development, childcare, and clinical services

● Ensure programs are delivered with fidelity, meet contractual and grant compliance requirements, and are staffed appropriately

● Lead operational planning for the Dolores Street four\-building shelter campus, including on\-campus service model design, vendor coordination, and readiness milestones

● Partner with program directors to develop and monitor performance metrics, client outcome data, and program quality indicators

**Grants \& Compliance**

● Supervise the Director of Grants \& Data and ensure organizational compliance with all federal, state, and private grant requirements

● Maintain working fluency in 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance; ensure TODN’s grant management practices meet audit standards

● Partner with the Controller and CEO on financial reporting obligations tied to grant awards

● Oversee the development and maintenance of internal controls, policies, and documentation systems that support grant compliance and organizational integrity

● Support grant renewals, reports, and new funding applications in coordination with the grants team and CEO

**Strategy \& Organizational Development**

● Translate the CEO’s strategic vision and board direction into operational plans, timelines, and accountability structures

● Lead implementation of TODN’s strategic planning priorities using a quarterly planning and tracking system

● Lead a structural review of TODN’s organizational design — assessing reporting lines, spans of control, role clarity, and departmental alignment — and present findings and recommendations to the CEO and board

● Design and build organizational infrastructure — SOPs, internal controls, workflows, and systems — that supports sustainable scale

● Identify operational risks and lead mitigation planning; escalate board\-level issues to the CEO in a timely manner

● Support the CEO in board reporting by preparing operational updates, metrics dashboards, and risk summaries

**What We’re Looking For**

**You’ll thrive in this role if you:**

● Bring 7–12 years of progressive leadership in nonprofit, government, or human services operations, with demonstrated experience managing multi\-department or multi\-program organizations at comparable scale (150\+ staff preferred)

● Have strong working knowledge of federal grant compliance, including 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance, and a proven track record building and supervising senior\-level teams

● Have experience developing and implementing organizational infrastructure, SOPs, and internal controls

● Are an exceptional organizer and project manager — able to hold multiple complex workstreams simultaneously without losing momentum or detail

● Lead with high emotional intelligence; able to hold authority with compassion in a trauma\-informed environment where staff carry significant vicarious burden

● Interest to represent the organization at community events, government hearings, and other external stakeholder functions

● Communicate clearly and confidently in writing and in person, including with boards and external stakeholders

● Graduate degree in public administration, nonprofit management, social work, business, or related field

**Preferred**

● Background in human services, trauma\-informed care, housing, or behavioral health, with experience in homeless services or victim advocacy program management

● Familiarity with California nonprofit compliance requirements and California human resources laws

● Prior experience managing a capital project, facility expansion, or new site launch

● Kern County or Central Valley networks and community ties

**Compensation \& Benefits**

● Salary: $120,000 – $150,000 annually, commensurate with experience

● Comprehensive medical insurance for eligible employees and their dependents, effective the first day of the month following 30 days of continuous employment

● Dental and vision insurance

● 401(k) retirement

Education Program Director, Greater Good Education \#88470 About Berkeley
  
  

At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation \- driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full\-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  

Departmental Overview
  
  

The Greater Good Science Center at UC Berkeley (GGSC) studies the psychology, sociology, and neuroscience of well\-being and teaches skills that foster a thriving, resilient, and compassionate society. Over more than two decades, the GGSC has provided a bridge between scientists and the public, turning research findings into practical resources that support well\-being for all. Since its founding, the Center has highlighted the importance of building social connections not only within communities but across groups, offering practical strategies for overcoming bias and prejudice, expanding one's circle of care, and promoting diversity, inclusion, and belonging.
  
  

The GGSC's Greater Good Education (GGE) program provides education professionals with practical, scientific insights to help them integrate the science of well\-being and flourishing into their lives, schools, and classrooms. It draws on disciplines such as social\-emotional learning, mindfulness, character education, and related topics. GGE's goal is to help education professionals better understand the roots of kind, helpful \- or "prosocial" \- behavior and emotional well\-being, and how they can build those skills in themselves, their colleagues, and their students.
  
  

GGE resources include our pioneering Greater Good in Education website, which offers more than 350 actionable, research\-based practices and has engaged several million users; a suite of online courses that support student and educator well\-being; Greater Good articles that share the latest education\-related research and its practical application in classrooms and schools; and Greater Good Educators, a community of practice program that brings together educators from around the world to learn with and from each other about the keys to individual and collective well\-being in education.
  
  

The GGSC's organizational culture prioritizes independence, rigor, and the well\-being of its members. Staff members enjoy autonomy and flexibility while working in a culture that encourages teamwork, connection, and collaboration. The GGSC welcomes a diversity of experiences and perspectives to inform its work and strives to operate internally by the values that drive its public\-facing programs: empathy, compassion, joy, forgiveness, appreciation, and cooperation. Recognizing that the science we cover has been shaped by systemic biases and inequities, we aim to address and correct for these prejudices whenever possible.
  
  

Position Summary
  
  

This position serves as the Greater Good Education (GGE) Program Director, overseeing the program's mission to build kinder, happier schools where everyone belongs. This position leads the short\- and long\-term planning for GGE, shaping the program's goals, strategy, key activities, and funding model. Working closely with the GGSC's executive director, the Education Program Director manages fundraising for the program and ensures that the program's direction aligns with the GGSC's overall direction. This position supervises a team that includes the Associate Director, Program Coordinator, Director of Learning Communities, Director of Educational Partnerships, Marketing Specialist, and Communications Specialist.
  
  

The Education Program Director oversees all GGE program content, partnerships, and other activities, including training, evaluation, and communities of practice, while also overseeing the development of the new Greater Good Schools program, which focuses on integrating Greater Good values into the fabric of entire schools and districts. The successful candidate possesses extensive experience in K\-12 education and a strong grasp of the science of social\-emotional learning, mindfulness, character development, and other prosocial research in education. Additionally, this position requires an entrepreneurial spirit and a command of nonprofit strategy, development, and management.

**Location:** Remote, based in the SF Bay Area, Seattle, New York, or Washington, DC (US time zones)

**Travel:** Expectation of 20\-40% travel time between US, EU and India.


OpenFn is the Digital Public Good for public service automation \& AI orchestration. Our platform automates data exchange and digital workflows so that governments and NGOs can deliver public services more efficiently, achieve interoperability across fragmented systems, and scale critical public services across health, humanitarian, and government programs.


Our team, Open Function Group, the primary steward of this open\-source platform, is a lean, fully\-remote team of integration specialists, solution architects, and implementation consultants working across 15\+ countries.


We are not making marginal improvements to already comfortable lives. We are building the digital public infrastructure that allows governments to function, clinics to operate, and vulnerable populations to access services they depend on.


Supporting document (with ideas for fundraising against): https://www.openfn.org/blog/dpi\-ai


The role**We're hiring OpenFn's first Director of Fundraising to lead our organization’s fundraising efforts with major donors, foundations, and mission\-aligned funders who invest in Digital Public Goods, Digital Public Infrastructure, and social\-impact technology. We will always act in the public interest, never for private profit. We want investment which is aligned as such.**


To date, OpenFn's growth has come from delivering complex digital transformation and implementation projects, and from fundraising efforts our CEO has largely driven himself. As we invest more deliberately in philanthropic and institutional funding to complement our subscription revenue, we're looking for an experienced fundraiser to build this function from the ground up: developing a fundraising strategy, cultivating and stewarding relationships with foundations and major donors, and helping OpenFn secure the multi\-year support it needs to keep expanding access to public service automation.


You already have a network of relationships with foundations, funders, and philanthropists active in international development, Digital Public Goods, and technology for social good, and you know how to translate a mission into a compelling case for support. You're comfortable being both the strategist and the one making the ask: this is a foundational hire, so you'll build the playbook as you go rather than inherit one.


We believe some of OpenFn's biggest fundraising opportunities sit at the intersection of philanthropy and policy, for instance helping governments understand why workflow and AI orchestration are essential to resilient digital public infrastructure or articulating the influence that open platforms have on the concentration of power in a market. Prior experience in policy conversations around Digital Public Goods or ICT for Development, and a passion for understanding and addressing the macroeconomic forces that shape wealth inequality is a requirement.


What you'll be doing**Build our fundraising strategy**

* Develop and lead OpenFn's fundraising strategy across major donors, foundations, and other mission\-aligned funders
* Establish the processes, systems, and reporting cadence a growing fundraising function needs, since you will be OpenFn's first dedicated fundraising hire (see helpful pointers from Wayan Vota!)
* Set and track fundraising priorities in partnership with the CEO and leadership team

**Cultivate \& grow major donor and foundation relationships**

* Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with foundations, family offices, and individual major donors aligned with OpenFn's mission
* Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective funders, from first conversation through multi\-year commitment
* Represent OpenFn credibly and persuasively with senior funder audiences, translating our technical work into a compelling case for impact and support

**Develop compelling funding proposals \& materials**

* Write and coordinate proposals, funding narratives, and reports that clearly connect OpenFn's work to funder priorities
* Partner with the CEO and program teams to gather the impact data and stories that anchor a strong case for support

**Engage the policy \& DPG ecosystem (a plus)**

* Build relationships across the broader Digital Public Goods and Digital Public Infrastructure funding community
* Represent OpenFn in relevant policy conversations and convenings where doing so could unlock new funding relationships

**Report on progress \& sustain funder relationships**

* Track and report on fundraising pipeline, commitments, and funder engagement to the CEO and leadership
* Ensure funders receive timely, high\-quality communications and reporting that keeps them engaged for the long term

  

**Requirements**  

  

Required Qualifications* 10\+ years of experience in fundraising, development, or philanthropic partnerships, ideally within international development, global health, or technology\-for\-good organizations
* A demonstrated network of relationships with foundations, major donors, or other institutional funders active in social impact or technology for development
* A track record of securing significant gifts or grants and stewarding funder relationships over multiple years
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical, mission\-driven work into a compelling case for support for a range of audiences
* Strong project management and organizational skills, comfortable building process where none exists
* Ability to work independently and as part of a small, fully\-remote team
* Fluent, professional\-level English communication skills (written and verbal), with the ability to work effectively across a distributed, multicultural team
* Reliable access to a quiet, dedicated remote workspace with stron

Capital Strategy Meets Business Growth.

**Are you a strategic relationship builder who knows how to turn opportunity into action—and relationships into capital?**

Do you know how to move comfortably between founders, investors, corporate executives, funders, and strategic partners? Can you identify where capital and opportunity intersect, open the right doors, develop meaningful relationships, and help move high\-value opportunities from conversation to commitment?

If so, this may be your seat at the table.

**JPG Enterprises Consulting (JPGE)** is an emerging, woman\-led enterprise building a diversified ecosystem across strategic growth, capital, executive leadership, real estate, housing innovation, global health and impact, business development, and emerging ventures.

We are seeking a **Director, Partnerships \& Strategic Capital** to help lead the development of JPGE's strategic capital ecosystem—building relationships, partnerships, and capital pathways that support enterprise growth and the activation of high\-value opportunities across the JPGE portfolio.

This is not simply a fundraising role.

It is a **senior strategic growth and capital\-development role** for someone who understands that capital is most powerful when it is aligned with the right opportunity, relationship, structure, and strategic objective.

The Director will work closely with the Founder \& CEO and **Global Capital \& Development Group (GCD)** leadership to identify, cultivate, structure, and advance strategic capital and partnership opportunities across the enterprise.

**THE ROLE**

The Director, Partnerships \& Strategic Capital will lead the development of relationships and opportunities across the intersection of:

**Capital \+ Partnerships \+ Business Development \+ Strategic Growth**

The role is responsible for helping JPGE build a qualified capital pipeline, cultivate high\-value relationships, identify appropriate capital pathways, and convert strategic relationships into actionable opportunities.

The Director will operate at both the **relationship level and the enterprise strategy level**—representing JPGE externally while helping shape the systems, processes, and opportunity architecture required to support scalable capital development.

This includes relationships with investors, family offices, corporate partners, strategic collaborators, financial institutions, institutional funders, and other aligned capital sources.

The Director will lead a small **Partnerships \& Strategic Capital team**, providing strategic direction, coaching, prioritization, and accountability while remaining personally engaged in high\-value external relationship development and capital opportunities.

The Director is expected to be an **originator, strategist, relationship architect, and opportunity developer**—not simply a manager of an existing pipeline.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1\. Strategic Capital Development**

Build and manage a qualified pipeline of strategic capital relationships and opportunities aligned with JPGE's growth priorities.

This may include:

* Private investors
* Family offices
* Corporate capital
* Strategic investment partners
* Institutional capital
* Corporate sponsorships
* Financial and lending relationships
* Strategic financing partners
* Growth\-oriented funding relationships
* Other aligned capital sources

The goal is not simply to generate a large prospect list.

The goal is to build a **high\-quality relationship pipeline capable of producing meaningful strategic opportunities.**

**2\. Strategic Partnership Development**

* Strategic access

* Distribution
* Expertise
* Institutional credibility
* Business development opportunities
* Industry relationships
* Strategic resources
* Co\-development opportunities

Develop partnership concepts that create meaningful mutual value and advance JPGE's broader growth strategy.

Help determine the appropriate capital pathway for emerging opportunities based on:

* Strategic objectives
* Business model
* Capital requirements
* Opportunity readiness
* Risk and complexity
* Partner/investor fit
* Timing
* Growth potential
* Transaction or partnership structure

**4\. Convert Relationships Into Strategic Opportunities**

Move relationships through a disciplined progression:

**Relationship → Conversation → Qualified Opportunity → Strategy / Structure → Proposal → Commitment**

Opportunities may include:

* Investment
* Sponsorship
* Strategic partnership
* Financing
* Joint ventures
* Corporate collaboration
* Expansion opportunities
* Capital introductions
* Business development relationships
* Strategic alliances
* Other enterprise\-growth opportunities

The Director will be measured not only by activity, but by the quality and progression of opportunities created.

**5\. Enterprise\-Wide Capital Alignment**

Work across JPGE's ecosystem to understand where capital and strategic relationships can create the greatest value.

This may include collaboration with:

jobs.title: Executive Director, NWSL Foundation
jobs.description:
The National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) is one of the fastest\-growing professional sports leagues in the U.S., powered by 16 clubs and a deep roster of the world’s best players, and built on record\-shattering fan, media and commercial growth. Now in its 14th season, the league’s momentum continues to accelerate, with viewership and attendance numbers growing rapidly, social media fandom on the rise, team valuations massively increasing and new top sponsors investing in the NWSL brand. This unprecedented growth in audience, media reach, and franchise value reflects the NWSL’s expanding fan base and increasing dominance in the sports\-media landscape and popular culture.

  

The future of the NWSL is now — and we’re looking for world\-class talent like you to help us continue the momentum.

### **The Role**

**About the NWSL Foundation**


The NWSL Foundation exists to advance the health and longevity of women athletes by supporting women’s health research and convening and coordinating the women’s athletic health research ecosystem. The Foundation helps guide the research agenda to ensure critical questions are identified, research efforts are aligned across institutions, and findings are translated into practical insights and resources for the benefit of the public and women and girls who participate in athletics.


The Foundation’s role is not to replicate academic research or function primarily as a grantmaker. Instead, it serves as a field\-shaping platform—aligning researchers, practitioners, and funders; reducing redundancy; elevating rigor; ensuring practical application, and enabling research that meaningfully advances women athletes’ health, performance, and longevity.


Anchored by an initial endowment, the Foundation will operate with scientific independence, disciplined governance, and a clear focus on actionability.

**Role Overview**
=================


The Executive Director is the founding leader and public face of the NWSL Foundation. This role is accountable for setting and stewarding the research agenda, convening the ecosystem, and ensuring the Foundation earns credibility as a trusted leader in women's athletic health research.


The Executive Director is not expected to be a career researcher or a traditional frontline fundraiser. Instead, this role requires a leader who has worked closely with researchers, clinicians, funders, and institutional partners—and who understands what it takes to develop credible research agendas, synthesize complex information, and mobilize resources in service of impact.


The Executive Director must be equally comfortable engaging senior researchers and clinicians, league and club leadership, players, and donors. This role requires judgment, credibility, and the ability to direct complex, multi\-stakeholder conversations—not simply administer programs.


The Executive Director reports to the NWSL Foundation Board and partners closely with League leadership, including Sporting and High Performance, while preserving scientific independence.

### **What You Will Own \& Drive**


1\. Research Agenda Leadership \& Field Stewardship

* Own and steward the Foundation’s multi\-year research agenda, grounded in elite women athlete needs and informed by the global research landscape.
* Identify gaps, redundancies, and under\-resourced areas across women’s athletic health research.
* Guide prioritization of research questions to ensure relevance, rigor, and actionability.
* Serve as an authoritative voice in shaping norms, priorities, and standards across the field—drawing credibility from prior leadership experience at the intersection of research, sport, and institutions.


2\. Convening \& Ecosystem Coordination

* Design and lead flagship convenings, including an annual research symposium that brings together leading researchers, clinicians, practitioners, and funders.
* Facilitate alignment and collaboration across academic institutions that are currently operating in parallel.
* Create structured forums for debate, synthesis, and agenda validation.
* Position the Foundation as a coordinator and catalyst—not a competitor to academic institutions.


3\. Research Governance, Rigor \& Independence

* Establish and oversee research governance structures, including Research Advisory Committees and peer review standards.
* Ensure funded, endorsed, or elevated research meets high standards of scientific rigor and ethical integrity.
* Protect scientific independence while maintaining relevance to elite sport environments.
* Define clear criteria for when and how research may involve NWSL athletes.


4\. Actionability \& Translation

* Ensure research questions and outputs are designed to be usable in practice, not solely academic.
* Partner with High Performance and Medical leadership to pressure\-test relevance and applicability.
* Support responsible translation of validated research into guidance, frameworks, or insights—without compromising independence or competitive integrity.


5\. Athlete\-Involved Research Oversight

* Establish disciplined protocols for research involving NWSL players, prioritizing player welfare, consent, and trust.
* Evaluate when athlete participation meaningfully advances the research agenda.
* Coordinate closely with League leadership, clubs, and the Players Association as appropriate.


6\. Fundraising \& External Partnerships

* Lead fundraising to sustain and scale the Foundation’s agenda\-setting work, including major gifts, aligned corporate partnerships, and research\-restricted funding.

**The Role**


The Program Director for the Fidelity Charitable Catalyst Fund will lead the Fund’s state and local giving infrastructure work in the Deep South as well as its national grantmaking portfolio focused on donor engagement and education. This work aims to encourage individual donors to support promising nonprofits with limited access to philanthropic funding. Candidates need deep knowledge of the philanthropy ecosystem, particularly in the South, and ideally, donor\-advised funds and high\-net wealthy donors. The Catalyst Fund is a grantmaking program of Fidelity Charitable, led by its Board of Trustees and operating separately from Fidelity Charitable’s donor\-advised fund program. The Fund provides grants to intermediary organizations that encourage donors to give more to promising nonprofits and help nonprofits strengthen their fundraising capacity, confidence, and ability to engage donors. The Fund is focused on growing resources for nonprofits in the Southwest, Deep South, and Central Appalachia, as well as organizations serving communities of color and rural communities nationwide. Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not\-for\-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high\-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

 **Job Summary**


The Mass General Brigham Development Office represents a team of 450\+ vibrant, collaborative, and skilled fundraising professionals, including the Newton\-Wellesley Development Team which supports advancing care at Newton\-Wellesley Hospital in Newton, MA. Join us in our mission to transform the future of community healthcare. The Mass General Brigham Development Office offers excellent benefits and competitive salaries.  

  

To Apply:  

Applications must include a current resume and a cover letter detailing applicable experience and accomplishments.  

  

The Executive Director, Philanthropy (EDP) is responsible for developing and executing the comprehensive fundraising strategy for Newton\-Wellesley Hospital to achieve annual and long\-term philanthropic goals.
  

  

Reporting jointly to the Vice President of Development, System Philanthropy for Mass General Brigham and the President and Chief Operating Officer of Newton\-Wellesley Hospital, this leader oversees all fundraising programs, including annual giving, major gifts, gift planning, corporate and foundation relations, special events, donor stewardship, and campaign initiatives.
  

  

The Executive Director leads and develops a high\-performing fundraising team, cultivates strategic partnerships with hospital leadership, physicians, volunteers, donors, and community stakeholders, and advances a strong culture of philanthropy throughout the organization. The EDP also partners closely with the Managing Director of Salem Hospital to provide strategic oversight and coordination of shared services staff, ensuring alignment, collaboration, and operational excellence across both hospital development teams.  

  

This role is accountable for setting fundraising strategy, driving innovation and growth, managing budgets and operational performance, leveraging data and metrics to inform decision\-making, and ensuring compliance with all Mass General Brigham Development Office and institutional policies related to fundraising, prospect management, gift administration, and performance management.  

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
  

  

* Develops and implements a comprehensive philanthropic strategy aligned with Newton\-Wellesley Hospital's strategic priorities and Mass General Brigham Development goals.
* Achieves annual fundraising goals across major gifts, annual giving, grateful patient giving, planned giving, corporate and foundation relations, and special initiatives.
* Partners with hospital leadership and Mass General Brigham Development to identify, prioritize, and advance philanthropic opportunities that support clinical care, research, education, capital projects, and strategic growth.
* Builds and maintains strong partnerships with the Hospital President, senior leadership team, physician leaders, and volunteer leadership to advance a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.
* Provides strategic leadership and support to the Newton\-Wellesley Hospital Board and its committees, engaging members in fundraising, stewardship, and ambassador activities.
* Develops annual operating plans, fundraising forecasts, and budgets while ensuring responsible stewardship of philanthropic resources and adherence to organizational goals and industry best practices.
* Oversees all fundraising operations, administrative functions, financial reporting, donor stewardship, prospect management, and performance metrics for Newton\-Wellesley Hospital philanthropy.
* Establishes short\- and long\-term fundraising priorities and implements strategies across major gifts, planned giving, annual giving, grateful patient fundraising, corporate and foundation partnerships, special events, donor recognition, and campaign initiatives.
* Collaborates with finance, marketing and communications, patient experience, clinical departments, and other hospital and Mass General Brigham teams to integrate philanthropy into organizational priorities.
* Serves as the hospital's lead frontline fundraiser, managing a portfolio of principal and major gift prospects while developing cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies that result in transformational philanthropic investments.
* Personally solicits and closes significant gifts from individuals, corporations, and foundations in partnership with hospital and system leadership.
* Recruits, develops, and supports volunteer leaders and campaign volunteers, providing guidance on fundraising strategy, donor engagement, and philanthropic best practices.
* Represents Newton\-Wellesley Hospital within the community, serving as the primary philanthropic ambassador to donors, community organizations, corporations, foundations, and civic leaders.
* Leads efforts to strengthen and expand the hospital's grateful patient program through close collaboration with physicians, nurses, and clinical staff.
* Promotes strong physician and employee engagement in philanthropy, fostering participation in employee giving, grateful patient referrals, and other philanthropic initiatives.
* Ensures fundraising programs are data\-informed, donor\-centered, and aligned with evolving philanthropic best practices while continuously evaluating performance and identifying opportunities for growth. Take on other office\-wide duties at the request of Development leadership.

 **Qualifications**


Bachelor's Degree Related Field of Study required or Master's Degree Related Field of Study preferred.

Executive Director. Reports to: Board of Directors as a whole. Supervisory responsibility: all employees, directly or through designated supervisors; oversight of contractors and professional advisers within approved agreements. The President is the ordinary Board liaison, not a substitute for collective Board authority.

FLSA classification: Exempt only while the actual duties, salary basis, and applicable salary requirements meet a lawful executive or administrative exemption. CHWW shall document and communicate the classification under Handbook Section 1\.C. In the absence of a documented valid exemption, the position is nonexempt and all compensable time must be recorded and paid.

Position Summary

The Executive Director is CHWW's chief employed administrator and is accountable for the overall management, financial stability, safe and reliable water service, personnel, regulatory coordination, member service, and execution of Board policy. In a small rural utility, the role includes both management and hands\-on administrative work, filling reasonable operational gaps, and developing dependable backup systems. The Executive Director is expected to anticipate needs, bring material issues to the Board early, and obtain appropriate professional assistance rather than perform unlicensed work or assume unrestricted authority.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1\. Leadership, planning, and daily administration. Translate the mission and Board decisions into work priorities, procedures, budgets, and measurable objectives. Coordinate treatment, distribution, billing, customer service, finance, HR, technology, and administrative functions. Resolve cross\-department issues; assign work; monitor completion; and maintain continuity when staffing is limited. Recommend organizational improvements and sustainable service standards.

2\. Board and corporate governance. Prepare agendas, management reports, budgets, proposed policies, and decision materials with the President and Secretary\-Treasurer. Present accurate operational, financial, compliance, personnel, and risk information without obscuring adverse developments. Support meeting notices, elections, membership records, minutes, corporate filings, and required member communications while preserving the Secretary\-Treasurer's accountability. Implement approved actions and maintain an action\-item record. Obtain counsel's advice on governing documents, records requests, open\-government applicability, major transactions, and disputed authority. Maintain a current governing\-document and amendment register, distinguish charter requirements from ordinary bylaw quorum rules, and obtain legal review of election terms and adoption thresholds. Maintain complete approval records for each election, amendment, and corporate action.

3\. Financial stewardship. Develop annual operating and capital budgets and multiyear financial and asset\-replacement plans. Monitor revenue, cash flow, costs, reserves, debt service, covenant compliance, and budget variances. Coordinate bookkeeping, payroll, tax filings, financial statements, and the independent annual audit with qualified staff and advisers. Recommend rates, fees, deposits, and financial policies to the Board with supporting cost and affordability information; implement only lawfully adopted changes. Ensure invoices and payroll are accurate and timely, and maintain independent approval and reconciliation controls even when personally covering financial tasks.

4\. Funding, grants, and lender relations. Identify suitable financing, grants, technical assistance, and reimbursement opportunities. Coordinate applications, feasibility information, matching resources, environmental and procurement conditions, reporting, draw requests, and closeout. Track restricted funds and avoid commitments before required approval. Maintain productive relationships with lenders, grant administrators, and financial advisers. Do not promise funding or eligibility before verification or incur debt outside Board authority.

5\. Drinking\-water and environmental compliance. Maintain a complete register of the utility's facilities, permits, operating conditions, sampling and reporting duties, inspection findings, and renewal dates. Ensure adequate licensed treatment and distribution staffing and backup coverage appropriate to each system classification. Coordinate compliance with the Safe Drinking Water Act, applicable Florida DEP and other public\-health requirements, Northwest Florida Water Management District requirements, and other applicable authorities. Require qualified review of sampling, operational logs, consumer confidence reports, public notices, water\-use reports, cross\-connection control, and corrective actions. Track applicable lead and copper, PFAS, and other rule changes with qualified advisers, identifying each adopted requirement and its effective date. Oversee continuing service\-line inventory verification, updates, customer notices, replacement planning, and related funding documentation. Maintain current compliance and funding records.

6\. Operations and infrastructure. Oversee source\-water availability, treatment, storage, distribution pressure, water quality, metering, asset condition, preventive maintenance, inventory, fleet readiness, and water\-loss control through qualified staff. Review work orders, outages, repairs, inspections, alarm response, and maintenance backlogs. Plan timely replacement or expansion of wells, tanks, mains, pumps, controls, and other assets. Ensure current maps and asset records, physical security, appropriate easements and access, and reliable supply and repair arrangements. Do not promise fire\-flow capacity, system extensions, or new connections without technical and legal verification. OneQuest Health is a leading behavioral health organization committed to transforming America’s health through compassionate, evidence based mental health services. Read to Succeed Asheville/Buncombe (R2S) is the only Black\-led literacy organization in the region and the only organization holding MOUs with Asheville City Schools, Buncombe County Schools, and the Housing Authority of the City of Asheville. Founded in 2010, R2S delivers three core programs — K\-5 tutoring, early childhood literacy support, and community literacy access — reaching more than 5,000 families a year through tutoring, book distribution, trainings, and community events. **Position Summary**

R2S is seeking an experienced, organized, and relationship\-driven Director of Development to lead the organization's fundraising strategy and operations. This is a foundational role: it holds both the revenue strategy behind R2S's funding — deciding which funders and donors need what and when — and the detailed, ongoing administrative work required to secure, track, report on, and steward that funding. The Director of Development will take primary ownership of grants, donor and sponsor relationships, and fundraising campaigns, building systems and institutional knowledge that outlast any one campaign or grant cycle.

**Company Description**  

Habitat for Humanity of Forsyth County, established in 1985 on Christian principles, is dedicated to a vision where everyone has a decent place to live. The organization’s motivation is to unite people around the concept of “putting God’s love into action” along with others who are interested in helping those in need of improved shelter. Habitat Forsyth is an affiliate member of Habitat for Humanity International, founded in 1976\.


The Habitat model assists local hard\-working families who do not qualify for traditional mortgages to become homeowners. After meeting certain income, credit and rental history qualifications, future Habitat homeowners attend financial education and home ownership/maintenance classes. new_jobs.description:
Site: Newton\-Wellesley Hospital  

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not\-for\-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high\-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

 **Job Summary**


The Mass General Brigham Development Office represents a team of 450\+ vibrant, collaborative, and skilled fundraising professionals, including the Newton\-Wellesley Development Team which supports advancing care at Newton\-Wellesley Hospital in Newton, MA. Join us in our mission to transform the future of community healthcare. The Mass General Brigham Development Office offers excellent benefits and competitive salaries.  

  

To Apply:  

Applications must include a current resume and a cover letter detailing applicable experience and accomplishments.  

  

The Executive Director, Philanthropy (EDP) is responsible for developing and executing the comprehensive fundraising strategy for Newton\-Wellesley Hospital to achieve annual and long\-term philanthropic goals.
  

  

Reporting jointly to the Vice President of Development, System Philanthropy for Mass General Brigham and the President and Chief Operating Officer of Newton\-Wellesley Hospital, this leader oversees all fundraising programs, including annual giving, major gifts, gift planning, corporate and foundation relations, special events, donor stewardship, and campaign initiatives.
  

  

The Executive Director leads and develops a high\-performing fundraising team, cultivates strategic partnerships with hospital leadership, physicians, volunteers, donors, and community stakeholders, and advances a strong culture of philanthropy throughout the organization. The EDP also partners closely with the Managing Director of Salem Hospital to provide strategic oversight and coordination of shared services staff, ensuring alignment, collaboration, and operational excellence across both hospital development teams.  

  

This role is accountable for setting fundraising strategy, driving innovation and growth, managing budgets and operational performance, leveraging data and metrics to inform decision\-making, and ensuring compliance with all Mass General Brigham Development Office and institutional policies related to fundraising, prospect management, gift administration, and performance management.  

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
  

  

* Develops and implements a comprehensive philanthropic strategy aligned with Newton\-Wellesley Hospital's strategic priorities and Mass General Brigham Development goals.
* Achieves annual fundraising goals across major gifts, annual giving, grateful patient giving, planned giving, corporate and foundation relations, and special initiatives.
* Partners with hospital leadership and Mass General Brigham Development to identify, prioritize, and advance philanthropic opportunities that support clinical care, research, education, capital projects, and strategic growth.
* Builds and maintains strong partnerships with the Hospital President, senior leadership team, physician leaders, and volunteer leadership to advance a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.
* Provides strategic leadership and support to the Newton\-Wellesley Hospital Board and its committees, engaging members in fundraising, stewardship, and ambassador activities.
* Develops annual operating plans, fundraising forecasts, and budgets while ensuring responsible stewardship of philanthropic resources and adherence to organizational goals and industry best practices.
* Oversees all fundraising operations, administrative functions, financial reporting, donor stewardship, prospect management, and performance metrics for Newton\-Wellesley Hospital philanthropy.
* Establishes short\- and long\-term fundraising priorities and implements strategies across major gifts, planned giving, annual giving, grateful patient fundraising, corporate and foundation partnerships, special events, donor recognition, and campaign initiatives.
* Collaborates with finance, marketing and communications, patient experience, clinical departments, and other hospital and Mass General Brigham teams to integrate philanthropy into organizational priorities.
* Serves as the hospital's lead frontline fundraiser, managing a portfolio of principal and major gift prospects while developing cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies that result in transformational philanthropic investments.
* Personally solicits and closes significant gifts from individuals, corporations, and foundations in partnership with hospital and system leadership.
* Recruits, develops, and supports volunteer leaders and campaign volunteers, providing guidance on fundraising strategy, donor engagement, and philanthropic best practices.
* Represents Newton\-Wellesley Hospital within the community, serving as the primary philanthropic ambassador to donors, community organizations, corporations, foundations, and civic leaders.
* Leads efforts to strengthen and expand the hospital's grateful patient program through close collaboration with physicians, nurses, and clinical staff.
* Promotes strong physician and employee engagement in philanthropy, fostering participation in employee giving, grateful patient referrals, and other philanthropic initiatives.
* Ensures fundraising programs are data\-informed, donor\-centered, and aligned with evolving philanthropic best practices while continuously evaluating performance and identifying opportunities for growth. Take on other office\-wide duties at the request of Development leadership.

 **Qualifications**


Bachelor's Degree Related Field of Study required or Master's Degree Related Field of Study preferred.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
**About R2S**

Read to Succeed Asheville/Buncombe (R2S) is the only Black\-led literacy organization in the region and the only organization holding MOUs with Asheville City Schools, Buncombe County Schools, and the Housing Authority of the City of Asheville. Founded in 2010, R2S delivers three core programs — K\-5 tutoring, early childhood literacy support, and community literacy access — reaching more than 5,000 families a year through tutoring, book distribution, trainings, and community events. R2S centers children in Asheville and Buncombe County living in high concentrations of poverty, using evidence\-based, culturally responsive methods grounded in the Science of Reading.

**Position Summary**

R2S is seeking an experienced, organized, and relationship\-driven Director of Development to lead the organization's fundraising strategy and operations. This is a foundational role: it holds both the revenue strategy behind R2S's funding — deciding which funders and donors need what and when — and the detailed, ongoing administrative work required to secure, track, report on, and steward that funding. The Director of Development will take primary ownership of grants, donor and sponsor relationships, and fundraising campaigns, building systems and institutional knowledge that outlast any one campaign or grant cycle.

The ideal candidate is a confident grant writer and relationship\-builder who is comfortable owning a full development portfolio, from prospect research through stewardship, and who wants to help grow the funding base for the region's only Black\-led literacy organization.

**What You Will Do**

**Grants**

* Proactively research and identify new grant opportunities — foundation, corporate, and government — that align with R2S's mission, programs, and strategic priorities, building a pipeline that extends beyond the organization's current funder base.
* Own and maintain the organization's grants calendar, tracking upcoming deadlines, letters of inquiry, full proposals, and reporting due dates so nothing is missed and staff have advance visibility into what's coming.
* Write all grant applications, translating R2S's program model, outcomes, and community impact into clear, compelling proposals tailored to each funder's priorities and guidelines.
* Prepare all grant reports, working with program staff to gather accurate data and outcomes and presenting them in a way that builds funder confidence and supports renewal.
* Track grant requirements, restrictions, and expenditures throughout the life of each award, ensuring funds are used and reported in compliance with funder terms and internal budgets.

**Funder \& Donor Relations**

* Cultivate and deepen relationships with current and prospective funders, individual donors, and sponsors, serving as a consistent and trusted point of contact for R2S's funding community.
* Maintain donor and sponsor records and keep the donor database current, accurate, and organized so that giving history, contact information, and relationship notes are always reliable and accessible.
* Deposit and log all incoming donations promptly and accurately, ensuring gifts are properly recorded and reconciled.
* Send timely, personalized donor acknowledgments and thank\-you messages that reflect R2S's values and make funders feel genuinely seen for their support.
* Maintain and document institutional knowledge about funders, donors, and past proposals — history, preferences, prior asks, and relationship context — so that knowledge carries forward and doesn't leave with any one staff member.

**Fundraising Strategy \& Campaigns**

* Oversee the Resource Development Committee, setting agendas, keeping members engaged, and ensuring the committee's work stays connected to R2S's broader fundraising goals.
* Develop and execute fundraising campaigns from concept through close, setting goals, timelines, and messaging in coordination with organizational leadership.
* Research and secure sponsorships by identifying prospective business and community partners, building the case for support, and negotiating sponsorship agreements.
* Conduct proactive donor and sponsor outreach to open new relationships and grow existing ones, rather than waiting for opportunities to come to R2S.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and professional fundraising experience.
* A proven track record in nonprofit fundraising, including grant writing and grant reporting
* Direct experience managing a grants calendar and full grant lifecycle (research through reporting)
* Hands\-on experience with a donor CRM/database (Bloomerang preferred)
* Strong writing skills, with the ability to translate program impact into a compelling case for funders and donors
* Experience cultivating and securing sponsorships and donor gifts
* Highly organized, with strong follow\-through and comfort managing multiple deadlines and funder requirements at once
* Familiarity with Asheville/Buncombe County and Western North Carolina philanthropy, or a clear plan for building those relationships quickly
* Alignment with R2S's values of equity, asset\-based framing, and community dignity

**Position Structure**

This is a full\-time, exempt position with a salary of $70,000 annually, plus benefits.

**Timeline**

Applications will be accepted through September 30, 2026\.

**To Apply**

Please send a resume and cover letter describing your fundraising and grant\-writing experience, your demonstrated results, and your interest in R2S's mission to admin@r2sasheville.org.

Pay: $70,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Work Location: In person
